dedupe_keys.name: euris inland fairway graph and fis euris inland waterway network dataset europe

description: Two related Zenodo datasets turn the European River Information Services (EuRIS) data into routable networks for inland waterway transport modelling. The EURIS Inland Fairway Graph aggregates the national waterway data served by the EuRIS portal web services into a graph in which fairway sections are edges and junctions or points of interest are nodes, merges co-located nodes and links national networks at border points into one pan-European graph. The FIS-EURIS Inland Waterway Network Dataset combines that backbone, covering thirteen or more countries with basic dimensions and CEMT classes, with the Dutch Fairway Information System (vaarweginformatie.nl), which adds water levels and flow velocities, bathymetric profiles and navigable depths, and details of locks, bridges and berths for the Netherlands and the Rhine corridor. Coverage is continental. Both are free under CC BY 4.0 and available to download as GeoJSON, GeoParquet, GeoPackage and Python pickle graphs; they are produced by Rijkswaterstaat staff with Deltares and partners (graph version 0.2.1, January 2026; network dataset June 2026). Caveats: they are research extracts that must not be used for navigation, and only the Dutch part carries detailed attributes. They are built for macroscopic traffic assignment, discrete-event simulation of locks and bridges with tools such as OpenTNSim, and bottleneck and connectivity analysis. They complement the Danube FIS Portal and are related to OpenTNSim.
